findings.title: The app imports are all started eagerly, not on demand
findings.body: Each `import("./...")` expression is executed while this module is initialized, so importing `@calcom/app-store` immediately starts loading and evaluating every calendar, video, CRM, and payment app. Awaiting a single entry later does not make the other entries lazy. This defeats the expected per-integration loading benefit and can create substantial startup CPU, memory, and chunk-loading contention for requests that use only one integration. Store memoized loader functions (for example, `() => import("./applecalendar")`) and invoke only the requested loader instead.

findings.title: Calendar deletions are launched in unobserved async callbacks
findings.body: `forEach` does not await the promises returned by its async callback. After the new `await getCalendar(...)`, this function proceeds to send the reschedule email and returns while module loading and remote calendar/video deletion are still pending. Rejections from either the dynamic import or `deleteEvent` also bypass the surrounding `try/catch`, resulting in unhandled failures and potentially leaving the old external event intact after the booking is marked cancelled. Build a `map` of deletion promises and await `Promise.all` (or `Promise.allSettled`) inside the error handling block.

findings.title: Calendar deletions are launched in unobserved async callbacks
findings.body: `forEach` ignores the async callback promises. The new `await getCalendar(...)` means this reschedule operation can send its email and return before the calendar module has loaded or the old external event has been deleted. Any import or deletion rejection is outside the enclosing `try/catch`, so failures are unhandled and the booking can be cancelled internally while its external calendar event remains. Await a collected set of deletion promises rather than using async `forEach`.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation does not wait for dynamically loaded calendar deletions
findings.body: The recurring-booking branch starts async `forEach` callbacks but never retains or awaits their promises. Since each callback now first awaits `getCalendar`, `apiDeletes` can be snapshotted by the later `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` before any remote deletion is even added to it. The handler can therefore delete local references and return success while recurring calendar events are still pending or fail with unhandled errors. Replace this loop with awaited per-credential/per-booking deletion promises and include those promises directly in the final wait.

findings.title: Reschedule mutation returns before external deletion callbacks complete
findings.body: The async callbacks passed to `forEach` are not awaited. With `await getCalendar(...)` added here, the mutation marks the booking cancelled, sends the reschedule email, and can complete before the calendar module resolves and before the old calendar/video event is deleted. Rejections from the dynamic import or deletion also have no error handler. Collect these operations with `map` and await them before sending the success path, with explicit error handling.
